text: Under lexical scope, what does `apply` pass as the new environment's parent?
choices: The environment where the procedure was defined, so a body's names mean what they meant where it was written.
The environment of whoever called, so names resolve against the caller's bindings.
The environment in which the argument expressions were evaluated.
A fresh empty environment, so a procedure can see only its own parameters.
explanation: That is the entire difference between lexical and dynamic scope, and it is one argument in `apply`. Every mainstream language chose lexical because it lets you read a procedure and know what its names mean from the text alone; under dynamic scope the meaning of a body depends on every call site, including ones written later by other people. Early Lisp was dynamically scoped partly by accident, since the caller's environment is already at hand.
